title: A Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Publication
extended_summary:
This paper is an editorial policy statement responding to the rapid emergence of ChatGPT and related generative AI tools in academic publishing. It argues that generative AI raises concerns about plagiarism, authorship, factual errors, fabricated references, and the weakening of scholarly expertise if authors rely on AI to produce substantive parts of manuscripts.

The paper does not report an intervention study or empirical evaluation. Instead, it proposes a journal-level policy: Culture, Education, and Future will reject manuscripts that are substantively aided by generative AI software, and may rescind papers later discovered to have used such tools inappropriately. The editorial also notes that the journal will use AI detection software, but will consult with authors because such detectors can produce errors.

The context is higher education and scholarly publishing, with some mention that the concerns also apply to high school students. The main conclusion is that generative AI should not be treated as an author or substitute writer in academic work; the journal prioritizes plagiarism prevention, research quality, and human control over scholarly content while remaining open to future, better-understood uses of AI.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial/policy essay rather than an empirical study. It presents normative arguments about generative AI in publishing and does not report a research design, sample, or outcome data.
impact_tier_rationale: There are no measured educational impacts or intervention effects. The paper addresses institutional policy considerations only, with no evidence of effect size or student-level outcomes.
